notes:
Inbound SMB self-serve signup. User reached out via contact form asking only about data retention / prompt storage -- high frequency of data-privacy questions from their legal/compliance team.

Initial context: Bridgecrest builds a lightweight customer support orchestration layer; plans to use Redwood hosted API for agent-assist + contextual search. Not high throughput today (50-200 API calls/min peak per workspace), but very cost sensitive — prototype budget estimated ~ $800-2,000/mo.

Key ask (paraphrased): "Where do you log prompts and responses? Can customers opt out of having prompts stored or used for model training? What are retention defaults and can they be shortened or disabled?"

Security/compliance notes: legal requested clear statements on: training data usage (explicit deny), ability to purge historical logs on demand, retention windows per-account, and audit trails for deletion. Also asked whether logs are stored in plaintext in backups and how long telemetry/metrics are kept. Region: prefer AWS us-east-1; data residency not strict but would like reassurance.

Model/architecture preferences: prefer open-model-compatible endpoints but currently OK with Redwood-managed curated models (hosted). Want explicit promise: no training on customer data, ability to opt-out of logging, and configurable retention.

Price sensitivity: several mentions of unit token cost and the effect of long retention on billing forecasts.

Conversation excerpts: 
- AE (Alex): "We can offer hosted API with account-level retention controls + 30d default, shorter on request" — flagged by the SE for confirmation.
- Customer (Head of Legal): "We need to see a policy and an admin control to toggle logging — can't proceed to POC without it."

POC ask: 2-week trial using hosted_api in us-east-1, sample traffic (synthetic) to validate latency and retention controls. Will need an example retention_config and API header for opt-out.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Sent quick reply with privacy FAQ stub and pricing link (Gmail thread above).
- Opened INF-2398 to track SE tasks: share retention options + config snippet.
- Assigned SE (Priya) to scope POC and produce short runbook for how to toggle opt-out and verify deletion.

Notes on tone: customer is pragmatic, not enterprise-locked — wants clear, simple controls and legal text they can paste into vendor questionnaire. Will move quickly if answers are clear and low-friction.
